formulas.description: Conservation of energy in single-photon photo-electron emission and stopping potential $V_0$.
formulas.explanation: Explains why photoelectron emission occurs with zero detectable time lag ($< 10^{-9}\text{ s}$) and why emission stops entirely below threshold frequency $\nu_0$ regardless of light intensity.

formulas.title: de Broglie Wavelength of Matter Waves
formulas.derivation: Louis de Broglie hypothesized nature is symmetric: if photons have momentum $p = E/c = h\nu/c = h/\lambda$, matter particles must carry wavelength $\lambda = h/p$. For non-relativistic particle accelerated through voltage $V$: $K = qV = \frac{p^2}{2m} \implies p = \sqrt{2mqV}$. Hence $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}}$. For electron ($m = 9.109 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}, q = 1.602 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$), this evaluates to $\lambda = \frac{1.227}{\sqrt{V}}\text{ nm}$.
formulas.description: Wave-particle duality wavelength associated with any material particle of momentum p.
formulas.explanation: Confirmed experimentally by Davisson-Germer electron diffraction on nickel crystals; forms the basis of electron microscopy.

formulas.title: Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle
formulas.derivation: Follows from Fourier transform properties of wavepackets: spatial width $\Delta x$ and wavenumber spread $\Delta k$ obey $\Delta x \Delta k \ge 1/2$. Using de Broglie relation $p = \hbar k \implies \Delta p = \hbar \Delta k$, multiplying by $\hbar$ yields $\Delta x \Delta p_x \ge \hbar / 2$.
formulas.description: Fundamental quantum limit on simultaneous measurement precision of conjugate variables.
formulas.explanation: Strict quantum mechanical property; proves why electrons cannot exist inside atomic nuclei.

formulas.latex: r_n = \frac{n^2 h^2 \epsilon_0}{\pi m e^2 Z} = \frac{n^2}{Z} a_0, \quad a_0 \approx 0.529 \text{ \AA}
formulas.title: Bohr Atomic Model: Orbital Radii
formulas.derivation: Bohr's quantization postulate: $m v r = \frac{n h}{2\pi} \implies v = \frac{n h}{2\pi m r}$. Coulomb force supplies centripetal force: $\frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\frac{Z e^2}{r^2} = \frac{m v^2}{r} = \frac{m}{r}\left(\frac{n h}{2\pi m r}\right)^2 = \frac{n^2 h^2}{4\pi^2 m r^3}$. Solving for $r$: $r_n = \frac{\epsilon_0 n^2 h^2}{\pi m Z e^2} = \frac{n^2}{Z} a_0$.
formulas.description: Quantized orbital radii of hydrogen-like single-electron atoms.
formulas.explanation: Orbital radius scales as $n^2 / Z$.

formulas.latex: E_n = -\frac{m Z^2 e^4}{8 \epsilon_0^2 h^2 n^2} = -13.6 \frac{Z^2}{n^2} \text{ eV}
formulas.title: Bohr Atomic Model: Quantized Energy Levels
formulas.derivation: Kinetic energy: $K = \frac{1}{2}m v^2 = \frac{1}{8\pi\epsilon_0}\frac{Z e^2}{r}$. Potential energy: $U = -\frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\frac{Z e^2}{r}$. Total energy: $E = K + U = -\frac{1}{8\pi\epsilon_0}\frac{Z e^2}{r} = -K = \frac{1}{2}U$. Substituting orbital radius $r_n$: $E_n = -\frac{m Z^2 e^4}{8\epsilon_0^2 h^2 n^2} = -13.6 \frac{Z^2}{n^2}\text{ eV}$.
formulas.description: Total discrete energy levels of bound electron in hydrogenic atom.
formulas.explanation: Negative sign signifies bound state. Ground state of hydrogen ($n=1, Z=1$) has ionization energy $13.6\text{ eV}$.

formulas.title: Rydberg Formula for Hydrogen Spectral Series

variables.n_1, n_2: Lower and higher energy quantum numbers ($n_2 > n_1$)

formulas.derivation: Conservation of energy: $E_{photon} = h\nu = \frac{hc}{\lambda} = E_{n_2} - E_{n_1} = \frac{m Z^2 e^4}{8\epsilon_0^2 h^2}\left(\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2}\right)$. Dividing by $hc$: $\frac{1}{\lambda} = \left(\frac{m e^4}{8\epsilon_0^2 h^3 c}\right) Z^2 \left(\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2}\right) = R_H Z^2 \left(\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2}\right)$.
formulas.description: Wavenumber of photon emitted or absorbed during electron transition between quantum states $n_2 \to n_1$.
formulas.explanation: Lyman series ($n_1=1$, Ultraviolet); Balmer series ($n_1=2$, Visible); Paschen series ($n_1=3$, Infrared); Brackett ($n_1=4$); Pfund ($n_1=5$).

formulas.latex: N(t) = N_0 e^{-\lambda t} = N_0 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t / T_{1/2}}, \quad T_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{\lambda} \approx \frac{0.693}{\lambda}, \quad \tau = \frac{1}{\lambda}
formulas.title: Law of Radioactive Decay
formulas.derivation: Rate of disintegration is directly proportional to present population: $-\frac{dN}{dt} = \lambda N \implies \frac{dN}{N} = -\lambda dt$. Integrating from $t=0$ ($N=N_0$) to $t$: $\ln(N/N_0) = -\lambda t \implies N(t) = N_0 e^{-\lambda t}$. At half-life $t = T_{1/2}$, $N = N_0 / 2$: $e^{-\lambda T_{1/2}} = 1/2 \implies \lambda T_{1/2} = \ln 2 \implies T_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{\lambda} \approx \frac{0.693}{\lambda}$. Mean life is $\tau = \frac{1}{N_0}\int_0^\infty N(t)dt = \frac{1}{\lambda}$.
formulas.description: Exponential disintegration of unstable radionuclides, half-life $T_{1/2}$, and mean lifetime $\tau$.
formulas.explanation: Activity is $A(t) = -dN/dt = \lambda N(t) = A_0 e^{-\lambda t}$; 1 Becquerel (Bq) $= 1\text{ decay/sec}$, 1 Curie (Ci) $= 3.7 \times 10^{10}\text{ Bq}$.

formulas.latex: \Delta m = [Z m_p + (A - Z)m_n] - M_{nucleus}, \quad E_b = \Delta m \cdot c^2 = \Delta m (931.5 \text{ MeV/u})
formulas.title: Nuclear Mass Defect and Binding Energy
formulas.derivation: Free nucleons have greater combined rest mass than the bound composite nucleus. The missing mass $\Delta m = Z m_p + (A-Z)m_n - M$ was liberated as binding energy during nucleosynthesis following Einstein's mass-energy equivalence $E = \Delta m \cdot c^2$. Using $1\text{ u} = 1.6605 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}$ and $c = 3 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}$ yields $1\text{ u} \equiv 931.5\text{ MeV}$.
formulas.description: Mass converted into binding energy holding nucleons together within the nucleus.
formulas.explanation: Binding energy per nucleon curve peaks near Iron-56 ($E_b/A \approx 8.8\text{ MeV/nucleon}$), explaining why light nuclei undergo nuclear fusion and heavy nuclei undergo nuclear fission.

formulas.latex: R = R_0 A^{1/3}, \quad R_0 \approx 1.2 \times 10^{-15} \text{ m} = 1.2 \text{ fm}, \quad \rho_{nuclear} \approx 2.3 \times 10^{17} \text{ kg/m}^3
formulas.title: Nuclear Radius and Constant Nuclear Density
formulas.derivation: High-energy electron scattering experiments demonstrate nuclear volume is directly proportional to number of nucleons $A$: $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 \propto A \implies R = R_0 A^{1/3}$. Nuclear mass is $M \approx A m_N$. Density is $\rho = \frac{M}{V} = \frac{A m_N}{\frac{4}{3}\pi R_0^3 A} = \frac{3 m_N}{4\pi R_0^3} = \text{constant} \approx 2.3 \times 10^{17}\text{ kg/m}^3$.
formulas.description: Nuclear size scaling with mass number A and universal nuclear matter density.
formulas.explanation: Nuclear density is invariant across the entire periodic table, independent of atomic number.

formulas.latex: n_i^2 = n_e n_h \quad (\text{Mass Action Law}), \quad I = I_0 (e^{e V / \eta k_B T} - 1) \quad (\text{Diode Equation})
formulas.title: Semiconductor Mass Action Law and Shockley Diode Equation
formulas.derivation: Law of Mass Action: thermal generation rate of electron-hole pairs equals recombination rate $R = r n_e n_h$. In thermal equilibrium, generation equals recombination, yielding $n_e n_h = n_i^2$, valid for both intrinsic and doped extrinsic semiconductors. Shockley diode equation follows from Boltzmann diffusion of majority carriers across depletion barrier: $I = I_0(e^{eV / \eta k_B T} - 1)$.
formulas.description: Carrier concentration product in thermal equilibrium and I-V characteristic of p-n junction diode.
formulas.explanation: For n-type semiconductor ($n_e \approx N_D$), minority hole density drops to $n_h = n_i^2 / N_D$.

formulas.title: Bipolar Junction Transistor (BJT) Current Gains
formulas.derivation: By Kirchhoff's law on transistor: $I_E = I_B + I_C$. Dividing by $I_C$: $\frac{I_E}{I_C} = \frac{I_B}{I_C} + 1 \implies \frac{1}{\alpha} = \frac{1}{\beta} + 1 = \frac{1 + \beta}{\beta}$. Inverting yields $\alpha = \frac{\beta}{1 + \beta}$. Solving for $\beta$ gives $\beta = \frac{\alpha}{1 - \alpha}$.
formulas.description: Common-base current gain $\alpha$ and common-emitter current gain $\beta$ relations.
formulas.explanation: Small variations in base current produce large amplified collector current swings.

formulas.latex: V_{ripple} = \frac{I_{dc}}{2 f C} \quad (\text{Full-Wave Rectifier with Capacitor Filter})
formulas.title: Rectifier Ripple Voltage
formulas.derivation: Capacitor discharges through load resistor $R_L$ between successive rectification peaks for duration $\Delta t \approx T/2 = \frac{1}{2f}$. Charge lost is $\Delta Q = I_{dc} \Delta t = \frac{I_{dc}}{2f}$. Ripple voltage is $\Delta V = \frac{\Delta Q}{C} = \frac{I_{dc}}{2f C} = \frac{V_{dc}}{2f R_L C}$.
formulas.description: Peak-to-peak AC ripple voltage across capacitor filter in full-wave rectifier.
formulas.explanation: Ripple is halved compared to half-wave rectifier ($\frac{I_{dc}}{f C}$); higher capacitance yields smoother DC output.

formulas.title: Duane-Hunt Law for Continuous X-Ray Cutoff
formulas.derivation: Electrons strike heavy metal target (Tungsten/Molybdenum) after gaining kinetic energy $K = e V_a$. When an incoming electron loses 100% of its kinetic energy in a single braking deceleration impact with target nucleus, the emitted Bremsstrahlung photon carries maximum energy: $h\nu_{max} = \frac{hc}{\lambda_{min}} = e V_a$. Solving for $\lambda_{min}$ yields $\lambda_{min} = \frac{hc}{e V_a} = \frac{1240}{V_a}\text{ nm}$.
formulas.description: Shortest wavelength limit of Bremsstrahlung continuous X-ray spectrum at accelerating potential $V_a$.
formulas.explanation: Depends strictly on accelerating tube voltage $V_a$ and is completely independent of target anode material.

formulas.latex: \sqrt{\nu} = a(Z - b) \quad (\text{Moseley's Law for Characteristic X-Rays})
formulas.title: Moseley's Law
formulas.derivation: Henry Moseley (1913) analyzed characteristic X-ray transitions: an inner $K$-shell vacancy is screened by remaining electron, so effective nuclear charge seen by transition electron is $Z_{eff} = Z - 1$. Applying Bohr formula: $\nu = R_H c (Z - 1)^2 \left(\frac{1}{1^2} - \frac{1}{2^2}\right) = \frac{3}{4}R_H c (Z - 1)^2$. Taking square root: $\sqrt{\nu} = \sqrt{\frac{3}{4}R_H c}(Z - 1) = a(Z - 1)$.
formulas.description: Linear relationship between square root of characteristic X-ray line frequency and nuclear atomic number Z.
formulas.explanation: Historical breakthrough proving the periodic table must be ordered by atomic number $Z$ (nuclear proton count), not atomic weight.

catalog_formula_sheets.name: Relations and Functions Formula Sheet
catalog_formula_sheets.derivation: Divide $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$ by $a$: $x^2 + \frac{b}{a}x = -\frac{c}{a}$. Complete square by adding $\left(\frac{b}{2a}\right)^2$: $\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 = \frac{b^2 - 4ac}{4a^2}$. Taking square roots gives $x + \frac{b}{2a} = \pm \frac{\sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} \implies x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$.
catalog_formula_sheets.explanation: Yields the two exact roots of any general quadratic polynomial. The term $\Delta = b^2 - 4ac$ governs the nature of the roots.

formulas.title: Quadratic Formula for roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0
formulas.derivation: Divide $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$ by $a$: $x^2 + \frac{b}{a}x = -\frac{c}{a}$. Complete square by adding $\left(\frac{b}{2a}\right)^2$: $\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 = \frac{b^2 - 4ac}{4a^2}$. Taking square roots gives $x + \frac{b}{2a} = \pm \frac{\sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} \implies x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$.
formulas.description: Quadratic Formula for roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0
formulas.explanation: Yields the two exact roots of any general quadratic polynomial. The term $\Delta = b^2 - 4ac$ governs the nature of the roots.

formulas.title: Vieta's Formulas for Quadratic Equations
formulas.derivation: Since $\alpha, \beta$ are roots: $a(x - \alpha)(x - \beta) = a(x^2 - (\alpha + \beta)x + \alpha\beta) = ax^2 - a(\alpha + \beta)x + a\alpha\beta = ax^2 + bx + c$. Equating coefficients: $-a(\alpha + \beta) = b \implies \alpha + \beta = -b/a$, and $a\alpha\beta = c \implies \alpha\beta = c/a$.
formulas.description: Vieta's Formulas for Quadratic Equations
formulas.explanation: Directly links polynomial coefficients to root sums and products without solving the equation explicitly.

formulas.title: Difference of Roots Formula
formulas.derivation: Using identity $(\alpha - \beta)^2 = (\alpha + \beta)^2 - 4\alpha\beta = \left(-\frac{b}{a}\right)^2 - 4\frac{c}{a} = \frac{b^2 - 4ac}{a^2} = \frac{\Delta}{a^2}$. Taking principal square root gives $|\alpha - \beta| = \frac{\sqrt{\Delta}}{|a|}$.
formulas.description: Difference of Roots Formula
formulas.explanation: Measures the horizontal distance between the x-intercepts of the parabola $y = ax^2 + bx + c$.

formulas.title: Discriminant Characterization of Roots
formulas.derivation: Follows directly from the radical term $\sqrt{\Delta}$ in the quadratic formula. If $\Delta > 0$, $\sqrt{\Delta} \in \mathbb{R}^+$, yielding two distinct real values. If $\Delta = 0$, $\sqrt{\Delta} = 0$, giving coincident root $-b/(2a)$. If $\Delta < 0$, $\sqrt{\Delta} = i\sqrt{-\Delta}$, producing non-real conjugate pair $\frac{-b \pm i\sqrt{4ac - b^2}}{2a}$.
formulas.description: Discriminant Characterization of Roots
formulas.explanation: Determines whether the parabola intersects the x-axis at 2 points, touches at 1 vertex, or never intersects.

formulas.title: Condition for Exactly One Common Root Between Two Quadratics

variables.a_i, b_i, c_i: coefficients of a1 x^2 + b1 x + c1 = 0 and a2 x^2 + b2 x + c2 = 0

formulas.derivation: Let $\alpha$ be common root: $a_1 \alpha^2 + b_1 \alpha + c_1 = 0$ and $a_2 \alpha^2 + b_2 \alpha + c_2 = 0$. By cross-multiplication: $\frac{\alpha^2}{b_1 c_2 - b_2 c_1} = \frac{\alpha}{c_1 a_2 - c_2 a_1} = \frac{1}{a_1 b_2 - a_2 b_1}$. Eliminating $\alpha$: $\alpha = \frac{c_1 a_2 - c_2 a_1}{a_1 b_2 - a_2 b_1}$, so $\alpha^2 = \frac{(c_1 a_2 - c_2 a_1)^2}{(a_1 b_2 - a_2 b_1)^2} = \frac{b_1 c_2 - b_2 c_1}{a_1 b_2 - a_2 b_1} \implies (c_1 a_2 - c_2 a_1)^2 = (a_1 b_2 - a_2 b_1)(b_1 c_2 - b_2 c_1)$.
formulas.description: Condition for Exactly One Common Root Between Two Quadratics
formulas.explanation: Necessary and sufficient algebraic condition for two distinct quadratic equations to share a common solution.

formulas.latex: \Delta \ge 0, \quad a \cdot f(k) > 0, \quad -\frac{b}{2a} > k \implies \text{Both roots greater than } k
formulas.title: Location of Roots: Both roots greater than real number k
formulas.derivation: For both roots $\alpha, \beta > k$: (1) Real roots require $\Delta \ge 0$. (2) Parabola opens up ($a>0$) means $f(k) > 0$; opens down ($a<0$) means $f(k) < 0$, unified as $a \cdot f(k) > 0$. (3) The vertex $x = -b/(2a) = (\alpha + \beta)/2$ must lie strictly to the right of $k$: $-b/(2a) > k$.
formulas.description: Location of Roots: Both roots greater than real number k
formulas.explanation: Standard IIT-JEE test for restricting both roots of a quadratic polynomial to the right of a given real value k.

formulas.latex: a \cdot f(k) < 0 \implies k \text{ lies strictly between the roots}
formulas.title: Location of Roots: Number k lies strictly between roots
formulas.derivation: If $k$ lies between $\alpha$ and $\beta$, the vertex value must have opposite sign to $f(k)$ compared to $a$. If $a > 0$, parabola is below x-axis between roots $\implies f(k) < 0 \implies a f(k) < 0$. If $a < 0$, parabola is above x-axis between roots $\implies f(k) > 0 \implies a f(k) < 0$. Note: $\Delta > 0$ is automatically guaranteed since $a f(k) < 0 \implies b^2 - 4ac > 0$.
formulas.description: Location of Roots: Number k lies strictly between roots
formulas.explanation: Simplest root-location check: a single inequality $a f(k) < 0$ guarantees real distinct roots with k strictly between them.

formulas.title: Maximum or Minimum Value of Quadratic Function

variables.a: lead coefficient (min if a > 0, max if a < 0)

formulas.derivation: Let $f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c$. Setting derivative to zero: $f'(x) = 2ax + b = 0 \implies x = -b/(2a)$. Evaluating at critical point: $f(-b/2a) = a\left(\frac{b^2}{4a^2}\right) + b\left(-\frac{b}{2a}\right) + c = \frac{b^2 - 2b^2 + 4ac}{4a} = -\frac{b^2 - 4ac}{4a} = -\frac{\Delta}{4a}$. Second derivative $f''(x) = 2a$, so minimum if $a > 0$, maximum if $a < 0$.
formulas.description: Maximum or Minimum Value of Quadratic Function
formulas.explanation: Gives the absolute extremum of a quadratic polynomial. Range of $f(x)$ is $[-\Delta/4a, \infty)$ if $a > 0$ and $(-\infty, -\Delta/4a]$ if $a < 0$.

formulas.latex: a S_n + b S_{n-1} + c S_{n-2} = 0 \quad \text{where } S_n = p \alpha^n + q \beta^n
formulas.title: Newton's Sums Theorem for Powers of Roots

variables.S_n: linear combination of n-th powers of roots

formulas.derivation: Since $\alpha$ and $\beta$ satisfy $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$: $a\alpha^2 + b\alpha + c = 0$ and $a\beta^2 + b\beta + c = 0$. Multiply by $p\alpha^{n-2}$ and $q\beta^{n-2}$ respectively: $a(p\alpha^n) + b(p\alpha^{n-1}) + c(p\alpha^{n-2}) = 0$ and $a(q\beta^n) + b(q\beta^{n-1}) + c(q\beta^{n-2}) = 0$. Adding both equations yields $a(p\alpha^n + q\beta^n) + b(p\alpha^{n-1} + q\beta^{n-1}) + c(p\alpha^{n-2} + q\beta^{n-2}) = 0 \implies aS_n + bS_{n-1} + cS_{n-2} = 0$.
formulas.description: Newton's Sums Theorem for Powers of Roots
formulas.explanation: Extremely powerful JEE Advanced shortcut for computing high-power root expressions like $\alpha^{10} -  eta^{10}$ without calculating roots.

formulas.title: Sum of Cubes of Quadratic Roots
formulas.derivation: From algebraic identity $(\alpha+\beta)^3 = \alpha^3 + \beta^3 + 3\alpha\beta(\alpha+\beta)$, rearrange: $\alpha^3 + \beta^3 = (\alpha+\beta)^3 - 3\alpha\beta(\alpha+\beta)$. Substitute $\alpha+\beta = -b/a$ and $\alpha\beta = c/a$: $\alpha^3 + \beta^3 = (-b/a)^3 - 3(c/a)(-b/a) = -\frac{b^3}{a^3} + \frac{3bc}{a^2} = \frac{3abc - b^3}{a^3}$.
formulas.description: Sum of Cubes of Quadratic Roots
formulas.explanation: Allows fast computation of third-order symmetric root expressions using solely equation coefficients.

formulas.title: Condition for Positive Definite Quadratic Expression
formulas.derivation: Completing square: $f(x) = a\left[\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 - \frac{\Delta}{4a^2}\right]$. The squared term is $\ge 0$. For $f(x)$ to remain strictly positive for all $x$, the parabola must open upwards ($a > 0$) and its minimum vertex value $-\Delta/(4a)$ must be strictly positive, which requires $-\Delta > 0 \implies \Delta < 0$.
formulas.description: Condition for Positive Definite Quadratic Expression
formulas.explanation: Guarantees that a quadratic expression never crosses or touches zero, remaining strictly positive across all real numbers.

formulas.latex: c x^2 + b x + a = 0 \implies \text{roots are } \frac{1}{\alpha}, \frac{1}{\beta}
formulas.title: Transformation of Equations: Reciprocal Roots
formulas.derivation: Let $y = 1/x \implies x = 1/y$. Substitute into $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$: $a(1/y)^2 + b(1/y) + c = 0 \implies \frac{a}{y^2} + \frac{b}{y} + c = 0$. Multiply through by $y^2$: $c y^2 + b y + a = 0$. The roots of this transformed equation are $y_1 = 1/\alpha$ and $y_2 = 1/\beta$.
formulas.description: Transformation of Equations: Reciprocal Roots
formulas.explanation: Reversing the coefficients of a polynomial immediately inverts all its roots.

content_json.derivation: Divide $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$ by $a$: $x^2 + \frac{b}{a}x = -\frac{c}{a}$. Complete square by adding $\left(\frac{b}{2a}\right)^2$: $\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 = \frac{b^2 - 4ac}{4a^2}$. Taking square roots gives $x + \frac{b}{2a} = \pm \frac{\sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} \implies x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$.
content_json.explanation: Yields the two exact roots of any general quadratic polynomial. The term $\Delta = b^2 - 4ac$ governs the nature of the roots.

catalog_formula_sheets.name: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties Formula Sheet
catalog_formula_sheets.derivation: Bonding molecular orbitals concentrate electron density between nuclei, lowering system potential energy and stabilizing molecule. Antibonding orbitals contain a nodal plane between nuclei, increasing nuclear repulsion and destabilizing molecule by an equal/greater amount. Each bonding pair contributes $+1$ net bond, while each antibonding pair cancels one bond: $\text{Bond Order} = \frac{N_b - N_a}{2}$.
catalog_formula_sheets.explanation: Bond Order $> 0$ indicates a stable molecule; Bond Order $= 0$ indicates unbound species (e.g., $He_2$). Higher bond order correlates with higher bond dissociation energy and shorter bond length.

formulas.title: Molecular Orbital Bond Order

variables.N_a: Number of electrons in antibonding MOs
variables.N_b: Number of electrons in bonding MOs

formulas.derivation: Bonding molecular orbitals concentrate electron density between nuclei, lowering system potential energy and stabilizing molecule. Antibonding orbitals contain a nodal plane between nuclei, increasing nuclear repulsion and destabilizing molecule by an equal/greater amount. Each bonding pair contributes $+1$ net bond, while each antibonding pair cancels one bond: $\text{Bond Order} = \frac{N_b - N_a}{2}$.
formulas.description: Net chemical bond strength calculated from populations of bonding and antibonding molecular orbitals.
formulas.explanation: Bond Order $> 0$ indicates a stable molecule; Bond Order $= 0$ indicates unbound species (e.g., $He_2$). Higher bond order correlates with higher bond dissociation energy and shorter bond length.

formulas.title: Steric Number and Hybridization Formula

variables.M: Number of monovalent surrounding atoms (H, F, Cl, Br, I)

formulas.derivation: VSEPR postulates that valence electron pairs (bonding pairs and lone pairs) repel each other and position themselves as far apart as possible in 3D space to minimize electrostatic repulsion energy. Total electron domain count is $SN = \frac{V + M - C + A}{2}$. Hybridization state corresponds to: $SN=2 \implies sp$ (linear, $180^\circ$); $SN=3 \implies sp^2$ (trigonal planar, $120^\circ$); $SN=4 \implies sp^3$ (tetrahedral, $109.5^\circ$); $SN=5 \implies sp^3d$ (trigonal bipyramidal); $SN=6 \implies sp^3d^2$ (octahedral).
formulas.description: Determines electron domain geometry and atomic orbital hybridization according to VSEPR theory.
formulas.explanation: Repulsion hierarchy: Lone Pair-Lone Pair > Lone Pair-Bond Pair > Bond Pair-Bond Pair. Explains bond angle compression in $NH_3$ ($107^\circ$) and $H_2O$ ($104.5^\circ$).

formulas.title: Dipole Moment and Hannay-Smyth Equation for % Ionic Character
formulas.derivation: Electric dipole moment is vector $\vec{\mu} = q\vec{d}$ pointing from positive to negative center. Percentage ionic character is experimental ratio: $\% \text{ Ionic} = \frac{\mu_{observed}}{\mu_{purely\_ionic}} \times 100\%$. Hannay and Smyth developed empirical correlation matching experimental dipole data: $\% \text{ Ionic} = 16|\Delta\chi| + 3.5(\Delta\chi)^2$.
formulas.description: Molecular dipole moment and percentage ionic character estimated from electronegativity difference $\Delta\chi$.
formulas.explanation: When $\Delta\chi = 1.7$, bond is approximately 50% ionic and 50% covalent (Pauling boundary).

formulas.title: Formal Charge on Atom in Lewis Structure

variables.L: Number of non-bonding lone pair electrons
variables.V: Valence electrons in free neutral atom

formulas.derivation: Bookkeeping convention for electron distribution: the atom is assigned all of its non-bonding electrons ($L$) and exactly half of its shared covalent bonding electrons ($B/2$). Formal charge is free valence count minus assigned count: $FC = V - (L + B/2)$.
formulas.description: Apparent electrical charge assigned to individual atom assuming equal sharing of bonding electrons.
formulas.explanation: The most stable Lewis resonance structure minimizes overall formal charges and places negative formal charges on the most electronegative elements.

formulas.latex: U_0 = -\frac{N_A M z_+ z_- e^2}{4\pi\epsilon_0 r_0}\left(1 - \frac{1}{n}\right)
formulas.title: Born-Lande Equation for Lattice Energy
formulas.derivation: Total potential energy per ion pair is sum of long-range Coulomb attractive terms and short-range Born repulsive core potentials: $U(r) = -\frac{M z_+ z_- e^2}{4\pi\epsilon_0 r} + \frac{B}{r^n}$. Setting derivative to zero at equilibrium separation $r_0$: $\left(\frac{dU}{dr}\right)_{r_0} = 0 \implies B = \frac{M z_+ z_- e^2 r_0^{n-1}}{4\pi\epsilon_0 n}$. Substituting $B$ back into energy expression yields $U_0 = -\frac{N_A M z_+ z_- e^2}{4\pi\epsilon_0 r_0}\left(1 - \frac{1}{n}\right)$.
formulas.description: Theoretical lattice formation enthalpy of crystalline ionic solids.
formulas.explanation: High ionic charges ($z_+ z_-$) and small interionic radii ($r_0$) maximize lattice energy, leading to high melting points and hardness (e.g., $MgO$ vs $NaCl$).

formulas.latex: \Delta H_f^\circ = \Delta H_{sub} + \frac{1}{2}\Delta H_{diss} + IE + EA + U_{lattice}
formulas.title: Born-Haber Cycle for Ionic Solid Formation

variables.\\Delta H_{diss}: Bond dissociation enthalpy of nonmetal gas

formulas.derivation: By Hess's Law of constant heat summation, enthalpy change between initial elements in standard states ($Na_{(s)} + \frac{1}{2}Cl_{2(g)}$) and crystalline product ($NaCl_{(s)}$) is independent of path. Direct path is $\Delta H_f^\circ$. Indirect path vaporizes metal ($\Delta H_{sub}$), atomizes nonmetal ($\frac{1}{2}\Delta H_{diss}$), ionizes metal ($IE$), adds electron to nonmetal ($EA$), and condenses gas ions into solid lattice ($U_{lattice}$). Summing gives $\Delta H_f^\circ = \Delta H_{sub} + \frac{1}{2}\Delta H_{diss} + IE + EA + U_{lattice}$.
formulas.description: Hess's Law thermodynamic cycle calculating experimental lattice energy from thermochemical data.
formulas.explanation: Allows experimental determination of lattice energy $U_{lattice}$ and electron affinities that are hard to measure directly.

formulas.title: Fajans' Rules for Covalent Character in Ionic Bonds
formulas.derivation: Kasimir Fajans (1923) formulated rules governing covalent character in predominantly ionic bonds: high polarizing power of cation (high positive charge $z_+$, small radius $r_+$) and high polarizability of anion (large radius $r_-$, high negative charge $z_-$) maximize electron cloud distortion. Additionally, cations with pseudo-noble gas electron configurations ($18e^-$ outer shell, e.g. $Cu^+, Ag^+$) have higher polarizing power than noble gas ($8e^-$) cations due to poor $d$-electron shielding.
formulas.description: Criteria favoring polarizing distortion of anionic electron cloud by cation, introducing partial covalent character.
formulas.explanation: Explains why $AgCl$ is insoluble in water and partially covalent, whereas $NaCl$ is completely ionic and highly soluble.

formulas.title: Pauling Electronegativity Scale

variables.D_{AB}: Experimental bond dissociation energy of AB

formulas.derivation: Linus Pauling observed heteronuclear bond $A-B$ is systematically stronger than geometric mean of homonuclear bonds $A-A$ and $B-B$ due to ionic stabilization: $\Delta = D_{AB} - \sqrt{D_{AA} D_{BB}}$. Extra resonance energy scales with electronegativity difference: $\chi_A - \chi_B = 0.208\sqrt{\Delta}$ (where energies are in kcal/mol, or $0.102\sqrt{\Delta}$ in kJ/mol). Fluorine is assigned reference $\chi_F = 4.0$.
formulas.description: Difference in electronegativities based on extra ionic resonance energy of heteronuclear bond AB.
formulas.explanation: Fundamental scale for predicting bond polarity, reactivity, and acid-base character of oxides.

formulas.title: Mulliken Electronegativity Formula
formulas.derivation: Robert Mulliken (1934) reasoned that an atom's tendency to attract electrons in a chemical bond depends on how difficult it is to remove an electron ($IE$) plus how strongly it attracts an incoming electron ($EA$). The average is $\chi_M = \frac{IE + EA}{2}$. Empirical regression gives linear equivalence to Pauling scale $\chi_P = 0.336(\chi_M - 0.615)$.
formulas.description: Absolute electronegativity defined as arithmetic mean of ionization energy and electron affinity.
formulas.explanation: Mulliken scale is rooted in rigorous atomic properties, allowing computation of orbital electronegativities.

formulas.title: LCAO Approximation (Linear Combination of Atomic Orbitals)
formulas.derivation: Approximate molecular wavefunction by linear superposition: $\psi = c_A \phi_A + c_B \phi_B$. Applying Rayleigh-Ritz variational method to minimize energy expectation value $E = \frac{\int \psi^* \hat{H} \psi dV}{\int \psi^* \psi dV}$ leads to secular determinant $\begin{vmatrix} H_{AA} - E & H_{AB} - E S \\ H_{BA} - E S & H_{BB} - E \end{vmatrix} = 0$. For homonuclear diatomic ($H_{AA} = H_{BB} = \alpha, H_{AB} = \beta$): roots are $E_b = \frac{\alpha + \beta}{1 + S}$ (bonding) and $E_a = \frac{\alpha - \beta}{1 - S}$ (antibonding).
formulas.description: Construction of bonding and antibonding molecular wavefunctions and overlap integral S.
formulas.explanation: Because $\beta < 0$, bonding MO has lower energy than atomic orbitals; antibonding MO is destabilized by more than bonding is stabilized ($|E_a - \alpha| > |E_b - \alpha|$).

formulas.title: Vector Addition of Bond Dipole Moments
formulas.derivation: Dipole moments are 3D vector quantities directed along bond axes. By vector law of cosines, resultant magnitude is $\mu = \sqrt{\mu_1^2 + \mu_2^2 + 2\mu_1\mu_2\cos\theta}$. For linear symmetric molecules ($\theta = 180^\circ$, e.g. $CO_2, BeF_2$), $\mu = \mu_1 - \mu_2 = 0$. For symmetric trigonal planar ($\theta = 120^\circ$, $BF_3$) and tetrahedral ($CH_4, CCl_4$), vector cancellation results in net $\mu = 0$.
formulas.description: Resultant molecular dipole moment computed by vector summation of individual polar bonds at angle $\theta$.
formulas.explanation: Explains why symmetric molecules with highly polar individual bonds (like $CCl_4$ and $trans$-dichloroethene) are completely non-polar overall.

formulas.title: Schomaker-Stevenson Equation for Heteronuclear Covalent Bond Length
formulas.derivation: Simple additive covalent radii $d_{AB} = r_A + r_B$ overpredicts distances in polar bonds because partial ionic attraction pulls nuclei closer together. Schomaker and Stevenson (1941) introduced empirical correction proportional to electronegativity difference: $d_{AB} = r_A + r_B - c|\chi_A - \chi_B|$ where $c = 0.09\text{ \AA}$.
formulas.description: Calculates bond length $d_{AB}$ corrected for bond shortening due to electronegativity difference.
formulas.explanation: Demonstrates that ionic resonance shortens covalent bonds while simultaneously strengthening them.

catalog_formula_sheets.name: Binomial Theorem Formula Sheet
catalog_formula_sheets.derivation: By mathematical induction: Base case $n=1 \implies (x+y)^1 = \binom{1}{0}x + \binom{1}{1}y = x+y$. Inductive step: $(x+y)^{k+1} = (x+y)\sum_{r=0}^k \binom{k}{r}x^{k-r}y^r = \sum \binom{k}{r}x^{k-r+1}y^r + \sum \binom{k}{r}x^{k-r}y^{r+1}$. Shifting index and combining using Pascal identity $\binom{k}{r} + \binom{k}{r-1} = \binom{k+1}{r}$ yields $\sum_{r=0}^{k+1} \binom{k+1}{r} x^{k+1-r} y^r$.
catalog_formula_sheets.explanation: Expands any positive integer power of a binomial sum into an ordered series of n+1 terms where the powers of x decrease from n to 0 while powers of y increase from 0 to n.

content_json.title: Binomial Theorem Formula Sheet

sections.title: Binomial Theorem Formula Sheet - High-Yield Formulas

formulas.title: General Binomial Expansion for positive integer n
formulas.derivation: By mathematical induction: Base case $n=1 \implies (x+y)^1 = \binom{1}{0}x + \binom{1}{1}y = x+y$. Inductive step: $(x+y)^{k+1} = (x+y)\sum_{r=0}^k \binom{k}{r}x^{k-r}y^r = \sum \binom{k}{r}x^{k-r+1}y^r + \sum \binom{k}{r}x^{k-r}y^{r+1}$. Shifting index and combining using Pascal identity $\binom{k}{r} + \binom{k}{r-1} = \binom{k+1}{r}$ yields $\sum_{r=0}^{k+1} \binom{k+1}{r} x^{k+1-r} y^r$.
formulas.description: General Binomial Expansion for positive integer n
formulas.explanation: Expands any positive integer power of a binomial sum into an ordered series of n+1 terms where the powers of x decrease from n to 0 while powers of y increase from 0 to n.

formulas.title: General (r+1)-th term in binomial expansion

variables.r: index where r ranges from 0 to n

formulas.derivation: In the summation $(x+y)^n = \sum_{r=0}^n \binom{n}{r} x^{n-r} y^r$, the first term corresponds to $r=0$ ($T_1 = \binom{n}{0}x^n$), the second to $r=1$ ($T_2 = \binom{n}{1}x^{n-1}y$), and consequently the $(r+1)$-th term is directly given by $\binom{n}{r} x^{n-r} y^r$.
formulas.description: General (r+1)-th term in binomial expansion
formulas.explanation: Allows direct calculation of any specific term without expanding the entire polynomial. Essential for finding particular powers of x or constant terms.

formulas.latex: T_{middle} = \begin{cases} T_{\frac{n}{2} + 1} = \binom{n}{n/2} x^{n/2} y^{n/2} & \text{if } n \text{ is even} \\ T_{\frac{n+1}{2}} \text{ and } T_{\frac{n+3}{2}} & \text{if } n \text{ is odd} \end{cases}
formulas.title: Middle terms in binomial expansion
formulas.derivation: Total number of terms is $n+1$. If $n$ is even, $n+1$ is odd, so there is exactly one central term at index $\frac{(n+1)+1}{2} = \frac{n}{2} + 1$, corresponding to $r = n/2$. If $n$ is odd, $n+1$ is even, giving two central terms at positions $\frac{n+1}{2}$ and $\frac{n+3}{2}$ ($r = \frac{n-1}{2}$ and $r = \frac{n+1}{2}$).
formulas.description: Middle terms in binomial expansion
formulas.explanation: The middle term possesses the largest binomial coefficient $\binom{n}{r}$ in the expansion due to coefficient symmetry and unimodality.

formulas.latex: T_{indep} = \binom{n}{r} a^{n-r} b^r \quad \text{where } r = \frac{n p}{p + q} \text{ in } (a x^p + b x^{-q})^n
formulas.title: Term independent of x (constant term)

variables.r: integer value making net power of x zero
variables.p, q: powers of x in binomial terms

formulas.derivation: General term: $T_{r+1} = \binom{n}{r}(ax^p)^{n-r}(bx^{-q})^r = \binom{n}{r} a^{n-r} b^r x^{p(n-r) - qr}$. For the term to be independent of $x$, set exponent to zero: $pn - pr - qr = 0 \implies r(p+q) = np \implies r = \frac{np}{p+q}$. A constant term exists if and only if $r$ is an integer $0 \le r \le n$.
formulas.description: Term independent of x (constant term)
formulas.explanation: Finds the term with $x^0$. If $np/(p+q)$ is not an integer between 0 and n, no constant term exists in the expansion.

formulas.latex: r = \left\lfloor \frac{(n + 1)|y|}{|x| + |y|} \right\rfloor \implies T_{r+1} \text{ is numerically greatest term in } (x + y)^n
formulas.title: Numerically Greatest Term (NGT)

variables.r: integer index for maximum absolute magnitude term

formulas.derivation: Consider ratio of consecutive terms: $\left|\frac{T_{r+1}}{T_r}\right| = \left|\frac{\binom{n}{r}x^{n-r}y^r}{\binom{n}{r-1}x^{n-r+1}y^{r-1}}\right| = \frac{n-r+1}{r}\left|\frac{y}{x}\right| \ge 1 \implies (n+1-r)|y| \ge r|x| \implies r(|x|+|y|) \le (n+1)|y| \implies r \le \frac{(n+1)|y|}{|x|+|y|}$.
formulas.description: Numerically Greatest Term (NGT)
formulas.explanation: Identifies which specific term has the largest numerical value in magnitude for given numerical substitutions of x and y.

formulas.title: Sum of all binomial coefficients

variables.C_r: short-hand notation for binomial coefficient n choose r

formulas.derivation: Substitute $x = 1, y = 1$ into the binomial identity $(x + y)^n = \sum_{r=0}^n \binom{n}{r} x^{n-r} y^r$: $(1 + 1)^n = \sum_{r=0}^n \binom{n}{r} (1)^{n-r} (1)^r \implies 2^n = \sum_{r=0}^n C_r$.
formulas.description: Sum of all binomial coefficients
formulas.explanation: Total number of subsets of a set of size n, summing combinations of choosing 0, 1, ..., n elements.

formulas.title: Alternating sum of binomial coefficients
formulas.derivation: Substitute $x = 1, y = -1$ into $(x + y)^n$: $(1 - 1)^n = \sum_{r=0}^n \binom{n}{r} (1)^{n-r} (-1)^r = 0 \implies C_0 - C_1 + C_2 - C_3 + \dots = 0 \implies C_0 + C_2 + C_4 + \dots = C_1 + C_3 + C_5 + \dots = 2^{n-1}$.
formulas.description: Alternating sum of binomial coefficients
formulas.explanation: Shows that the sum of even-indexed binomial coefficients equals the sum of odd-indexed binomial coefficients, both equaling $2^{n-1}$.

formulas.latex: \sum_{r=1}^n r \binom{n}{r} = 1 C_1 + 2 C_2 + 3 C_3 + \dots + n C_n = n 2^{n-1}
formulas.title: Weighted sum of binomial coefficients
formulas.derivation: Differentiating identity $(1 + x)^n = \sum_{r=0}^n \binom{n}{r} x^r$ with respect to $x$: $n(1 + x)^{n-1} = \sum_{r=1}^n r \binom{n}{r} x^{r-1}$. Evaluating at $x = 1$: $n(1 + 1)^{n-1} = \sum_{r=1}^n r C_r \implies \sum_{r=1}^n r C_r = n 2^{n-1}$.
formulas.description: Weighted sum of binomial coefficients
formulas.explanation: Calculates the total number of element-subset pairs in combinatorics, representing the first moment of the binomial distribution.

formulas.title: Second moment weighted sum of binomial coefficients
formulas.derivation: From $n(1+x)^{n-1} = \sum r C_r x^{r-1}$, multiply both sides by $x$: $n x(1+x)^{n-1} = \sum r C_r x^r$. Differentiate again: $n[(1+x)^{n-1} + x(n-1)(1+x)^{n-2}] = \sum r^2 C_r x^{r-1}$. Evaluating at $x = 1$: $n[2^{n-1} + (n-1)2^{n-2}] = n 2^{n-2}[2 + n - 1] = n(n+1)2^{n-2}$.
formulas.description: Second moment weighted sum of binomial coefficients
formulas.explanation: Crucial for calculating the variance and second algebraic moments of binomial distributions in competitive mathematics.

formulas.title: Integral sum of reciprocal binomial coefficients
formulas.derivation: Integrate $(1+x)^n = \sum_{r=0}^n \binom{n}{r}x^r$ from $0$ to $1$: $\int_0^1 (1+x)^n dx = \sum_{r=0}^n C_r \int_0^1 x^r dx \implies \left[\frac{(1+x)^{n+1}}{n+1}\right]_0^1 = \sum_{r=0}^n \frac{C_r}{r+1} \implies \frac{2^{n+1} - 1}{n+1} = \sum_{r=0}^n \frac{C_r}{r+1}$.
formulas.description: Integral sum of reciprocal binomial coefficients
formulas.explanation: Standard calculus integration technique used to sum series where the denominator contains arithmetic progression factors.

formulas.title: Sum of squares of binomial coefficients
formulas.derivation: Consider $(1+x)^n(x+1)^n = (1+x)^{2n}$. Left side expansion: $(C_0 + C_1 x + \dots + C_n x^n)(C_0 x^n + C_1 x^{n-1} + \dots + C_n)$. The coefficient of $x^n$ is $C_0^2 + C_1^2 + \dots + C_n^2$. On the right side $(1+x)^{2n}$, the coefficient of $x^n$ is $\binom{2n}{n}$. Equating gives $\sum C_r^2 = \binom{2n}{n}$.
formulas.description: Sum of squares of binomial coefficients
formulas.explanation: Special case of Vandermonde's convolution identity, counting ways to choose n objects from two disjoint groups of n objects.

formulas.title: Vandermonde's Convolution Identity
formulas.derivation: Equating coefficient of $x^r$ on both sides of $(1+x)^m (1+x)^n = (1+x)^{m+n}$. On LHS: $\left(\sum_{k=0}^m \binom{m}{k}x^k\right)\left(\sum_{j=0}^n \binom{n}{j}x^j\right)$. Setting $j = r-k$ collects terms of power $x^r$: $\sum_{k=0}^r \binom{m}{k}\binom{n}{r-k}$. On RHS, the coefficient of $x^r$ is $\binom{m+n}{r}$.
formulas.description: Vandermonde's Convolution Identity
formulas.explanation: Fundamental combinatorial identity for evaluating cross-products of binomial coefficients across two independent binomial sets.

formulas.latex: (x_1 + x_2 + \dots + x_k)^n = \sum_{r_1 + r_2 + \dots + r_k = n} \frac{n!}{r_1! r_2! \dots r_k!} x_1^{r_1} x_2^{r_2} \dots x_k^{r_k}
formulas.title: Multinomial Theorem Expansion

variables.k: number of terms in base polynomial

formulas.derivation: Expand product of $n$ identical factors $(x_1 + \dots + x_k)$. Each term in the expanded polynomial is formed by choosing $x_1$ from $r_1$ factors, $x_2$ from $r_2$ factors, ..., and $x_k$ from $r_k$ factors where $\sum r_i = n$. The number of ways to choose these factors is given by the multinomial coefficient $\binom{n}{r_1, r_2, \dots, r_k} = \frac{n!}{r_1! r_2! \dots r_k!}$.
formulas.description: Multinomial Theorem Expansion
formulas.explanation: Generalizes the binomial theorem to polynomials with 3 or more terms. Total number of terms in expansion is $\binom{n+k-1}{k-1}$.

formulas.title: Binomial Expansion for Any Rational Index n
formulas.derivation: Using Maclaurin series expansion of $f(x) = (1+x)^n$: $f(0) = 1$, $f'(0) = n$, $f''(0) = n(n-1)$, $f^{(k)}(0) = n(n-1)\dots(n-k+1)$. By Taylor theorem: $f(x) = \sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{f^{(k)}(0)}{k!} x^k = 1 + nx + \frac{n(n-1)}{2!}x^2 + \dots$ By the ratio test, $\lim \left|\frac{a_{k+1}}{a_k}\right| = \lim \left|\frac{n-k}{k+1}x\right| = |x| < 1$ for convergence.
formulas.description: Binomial Expansion for Any Rational Index n
formulas.explanation: Extends the binomial theorem to fractional and negative powers (e.g. $(1+x)^{-1} = 1 - x + x^2 - x^3...$). Produces an infinite series valid strictly when $|x| < 1$.

content_json.derivation: By mathematical induction: Base case $n=1 \implies (x+y)^1 = \binom{1}{0}x + \binom{1}{1}y = x+y$. Inductive step: $(x+y)^{k+1} = (x+y)\sum_{r=0}^k \binom{k}{r}x^{k-r}y^r = \sum \binom{k}{r}x^{k-r+1}y^r + \sum \binom{k}{r}x^{k-r}y^{r+1}$. Shifting index and combining using Pascal identity $\binom{k}{r} + \binom{k}{r-1} = \binom{k+1}{r}$ yields $\sum_{r=0}^{k+1} \binom{k+1}{r} x^{k+1-r} y^r$.
content_json.explanation: Expands any positive integer power of a binomial sum into an ordered series of n+1 terms where the powers of x decrease from n to 0 while powers of y increase from 0 to n.

catalog_formula_sheets.name: Kinematics Formulas
catalog_formula_sheets.derivation: From definition of instantaneous acceleration $a = \frac{dv}{dt}$. Separating variables yields $dv = a \, dt$. Integrating both sides from $t=0$ (where $v=u$) to $t$: $\int_{u}^{v} dv = a \int_{0}^{t} dt \implies v - u = at \implies v = u + at$.
catalog_formula_sheets.explanation: Applies strictly when acceleration is constant in magnitude and direction along a rectilinear path.

sections.title: Kinematics Formulas - High-Yield Formulas

formulas.title: First Equation of Uniformly Accelerated Motion
formulas.derivation: From definition of instantaneous acceleration $a = \frac{dv}{dt}$. Separating variables yields $dv = a \, dt$. Integrating both sides from $t=0$ (where $v=u$) to $t$: $\int_{u}^{v} dv = a \int_{0}^{t} dt \implies v - u = at \implies v = u + at$.
formulas.description: Relates final velocity, initial velocity, constant acceleration, and elapsed time.
formulas.explanation: Applies strictly when acceleration is constant in magnitude and direction along a rectilinear path.

formulas.title: Displacement-Time Relation
formulas.derivation: Since instantaneous velocity $v = \frac{ds}{dt} = u + at$, we integrate $ds = (u + at)dt$: $\int_{0}^{s} ds = \int_{0}^{t} (u + at)dt = \left[ ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2 \right]_0^t = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$.
formulas.description: Calculates rectilinear displacement under constant acceleration over time t.
formulas.explanation: Yields net displacement, not total distance traversed if velocity reverses direction during interval $t$.

formulas.title: Velocity-Displacement Relation (Third Kinematic Equation)
formulas.derivation: Using chain rule for acceleration: $a = \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{dv}{ds} \frac{ds}{dt} = v \frac{dv}{ds}$. Rearranging: $v \, dv = a \, ds$. Integrating from initial $(u, 0)$ to final $(v, s)$: $\int_{u}^{v} v \, dv = a \int_{0}^{s} ds \implies \frac{v^2 - u^2}{2} = as \implies v^2 = u^2 + 2as$.
formulas.description: Relates final speed to initial speed and displacement without requiring explicit time.
formulas.explanation: Directly links kinetic energy change per unit mass to mechanical work done by constant force.

formulas.title: Displacement in the n-th Second
formulas.description: Distance traveled strictly between time $t = n-1$ and $t = n$.
formulas.explanation: Dimensionally valid because the implicit factor multiplying $(2n-1)$ is $1\text{ s}$.

formulas.title: Maximum Height of 2D Projectile
formulas.derivation: At maximum height, vertical velocity component vanishes: $v_y = 0$. Using $v_y^2 = u_y^2 - 2gH$ with $u_y = u\sin\theta$: $0 = (u\sin\theta)^2 - 2gH \implies H = \frac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g}$.
formulas.description: Peak vertical elevation reached by a projectile launched at angle $\theta$ with initial speed $u$.
formulas.explanation: Depends only on vertical launch velocity component $u_y$.

formulas.title: Time of Flight for Projectile Motion
formulas.derivation: Set vertical displacement $y = 0$ in $y = (u\sin\theta)t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$: $t(u\sin\theta - \frac{1}{2}gt) = 0$. Since $t=0$ is launch, landing time is $t = T = \frac{2u\sin\theta}{g}$.
formulas.description: Total duration projectile remains airborne before landing on horizontal ground.
formulas.explanation: Time of ascent equals time of descent ($t_{up} = t_{down} = \frac{u\sin\theta}{g}$) under symmetric vacuum trajectory.

formulas.title: Horizontal Range of Projectile
formulas.derivation: $R = u_x \cdot T = (u\cos\theta) \cdot \left(\frac{2u\sin\theta}{g}\right) = \frac{u^2 (2\sin\theta\cos\theta)}{g} = \frac{u^2 \sin(2\theta)}{g}$.
formulas.description: Total horizontal displacement traveled by a projectile on flat ground.
formulas.explanation: Maximum range occurs at $\theta = 45^\circ$ where $\sin(2\theta) = 1$. Complementary launch angles $\theta$ and $90^\circ - \theta$ give identical ranges.

formulas.title: Equation of Projectile Trajectory
formulas.derivation: From horizontal motion: $x = (u\cos\theta)t \implies t = \frac{x}{u\cos\theta}$. Substituting into $y = (u\sin\theta)t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$: $y = u\sin\theta\left(\frac{x}{u\cos\theta}\right) - \frac{g}{2}\left(\frac{x^2}{u^2\cos^2\theta}\right) = x\tan\theta - \frac{gx^2}{2u^2\cos^2\theta}$. Factoring out $x\tan\theta$ and noting $R = \frac{2u^2\sin\theta\cos\theta}{g}$ gives $y = x\tan\theta(1 - x/R)$.
formulas.description: Parabolic path equation relating vertical coordinates $y$ and horizontal coordinates $x$.
formulas.explanation: Standard quadratic trajectory form; useful for collision, clearing hurdles, and angle-of-elevation problems.

formulas.title: Relative Velocity in 2D/3D

variables.\\vec{v}_A: Velocity of A in ground frame
variables.\\vec{v}_B: Velocity of B in ground frame
variables.\\vec{v}_{A/B}: Relative velocity of A w.r.t. B

formulas.derivation: Position vector of A relative to B is $\vec{r}_{A/B} = \vec{r}_A - \vec{r}_B$. Differentiating with respect to time: $\frac{d\vec{r}_{A/B}}{dt} = \frac{d\vec{r}_A}{dt} - \frac{d\vec{r}_B}{dt} \implies \vec{v}_{A/B} = \vec{v}_A - \vec{v}_B$.
formulas.description: Velocity of object A observed from the reference frame of moving observer B.
formulas.explanation: Crucial for river-swimmer problems, rain-umbrella problems, and minimum approach distance calculations.

formulas.title: River Crossing Time and Drift
formulas.derivation: Cross-river speed component is $v_y = v_{br}\cos\theta$, so $t = d / (v_{br}\cos\theta)$. Net downstream velocity along bank is $v_x = v_r - v_{br}\sin\theta$. Drift is $x = v_x \cdot t$.
formulas.description: Time taken by boat to cross river of width d and resultant downstream drift.
formulas.explanation: Shortest time occurs when heading straight across ($\theta = 0, t_{min} = d/v_{br}$). Zero drift requires $\sin\theta = v_r / v_{br}$ (valid if $v_{br} \ge v_r$).

formulas.title: Centripetal and Tangential Accelerations in Curvilinear Motion
formulas.derivation: In planar polar coordinates, position $\vec{r} = R\hat{r}$. Velocity is $\vec{v} = R\omega \hat{\theta}$. Differentiating velocity: $\vec{a} = R\alpha \hat{\theta} + R\omega \frac{d\hat{\theta}}{dt}$. Since $\frac{d\hat{\theta}}{dt} = -\omega\hat{r}$, $\vec{a} = -R\omega^2 \hat{r} + R\alpha \hat{\theta} = -\frac{v^2}{R}\hat{r} + a_t \hat{\theta}$. Total magnitude $a = \sqrt{a_n^2 + a_t^2}$.
formulas.description: Decomposition of total acceleration into normal (direction change) and tangential (speed change) components.
formulas.explanation: Centripetal acceleration always points toward center of curvature; tangential acceleration alters the magnitude of velocity.

formulas.title: Radius of Curvature of Trajectory
formulas.derivation: At any point, $a_n = \frac{v^2}{R_c} = g\cos\phi$. From differential geometry, curvature $\kappa = \frac{1}{R_c} = \frac{|y''|}{(1 + y'^2)^{3/2}}$, thus $R_c = \frac{(1 + y'^2)^{3/2}}{|y''|}$.
formulas.description: Local radius of osculating circle for any planar curve $y(x)$.
formulas.explanation: Enables computing normal contact force and centripetal load on curved tracks and projectile apogees.

content_json.title: Chemical Thermodynamics Formula Sheet

sections.title: Chemical Thermodynamics Formula Sheet - High-Yield Formulas

formulas.title: Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction and Lenz's Law
formulas.derivation: Empirical discovery by Michael Faraday (1831). The negative sign (Lenz's Law, Heinrich Lenz 1834) enforces energy conservation: the induced current flows in such a direction that its own magnetic field opposes the original flux change that produced it.
formulas.description: Induced electromotive force in a circuit equals negative rate of change of magnetic flux through loop.
formulas.explanation: If flux increases, induced magnetic field points opposite to applied field; if flux decreases, induced field reinforces it.

formulas.title: Motional EMF in a Moving Conductor
formulas.derivation: Mobile conduction electrons inside rod experience magnetic Lorentz force $\vec{F}_B = -e(\vec{v}\times\vec{B})$. Work done moving an electron through length $\vec{l}$ is $W = \int \vec{F}_B \cdot d\vec{l} = -e \int (\vec{v}\times\vec{B})\cdot d\vec{l}$. Induced EMF is work done per unit positive charge: $\mathcal{E} = W/(-e) = (\vec{v}\times\vec{B})\cdot\vec{l} = B v l\sin\theta$.
formulas.description: Electromotive force induced across ends of a conducting rod of length l translating with speed v through magnetic field B.
formulas.explanation: Forms the foundation of electrical power generation in alternators and dynamos.

formulas.title: Rotational Motional EMF of a Rotating Rod
formulas.derivation: Consider element $dr$ at distance $r$ from pivot: linear velocity is $v(r) = r\omega$. Motional EMF generated across element is $d\mathcal{E} = B v(r) dr = B(r\omega)dr$. Integrating from pivot $r=0$ to tip $r=l$: $\mathcal{E} = B\omega \int_0^l r dr = B\omega \left[\frac{r^2}{2}\right]_0^l = \frac{1}{2}B\omega l^2$.
formulas.description: EMF induced between pivot and tip of a conducting rod of length l rotating with angular speed $\omega$ in perpendicular field B.
formulas.explanation: Also equals $B\left(\frac{dA}{dt}\right) = B\left(\frac{1}{2}l^2\omega\right)$, matching rate of area swept.

formulas.latex: L = \frac{N \Phi_B}{I} = \mu_0 n^2 A l, \quad U_B = \frac{1}{2}L I^2, \quad u_B = \frac{B^2}{2\mu_0}
formulas.title: Self-Inductance and Magnetic Energy Density
formulas.derivation: Inside solenoid, field is $B = \mu_0 n I$. Flux per turn is $\Phi = B A = \mu_0 n I A$. Total linkage is $\lambda = N\Phi = (nl)(\mu_0 n I A) = (\mu_0 n^2 A l)I$. By definition $L = \lambda / I = \mu_0 n^2 A l$. Work required to establish current $I$ against back-EMF $\mathcal{E}_L = -L\frac{di}{dt}$ is $U = \int P\,dt = \int (L\frac{di}{dt} i)dt = L \int_0^I i\,di = \frac{1}{2}LI^2$. Dividing by volume $V = Al$ and using $B = \mu_0 n I$ yields $u_B = \frac{B^2}{2\mu_0}$.
formulas.description: Self-inductance of solenoid, total energy stored in inductor magnetic field, and volume energy density.
formulas.explanation: Analogous to kinetic energy $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$ and electrostatic energy density $\frac{1}{2}\epsilon_0 E^2$.

formulas.latex: M = \frac{N_2 \Phi_{21}}{I_1} = \mu_0 n_1 n_2 A l, \quad M \le \sqrt{L_1 L_2}
formulas.title: Mutual Inductance and Coupling Coefficient
formulas.derivation: Current $I_1$ in outer coil produces uniform field $B_1 = \mu_0 n_1 I_1$. Flux passing through each turn of inner coil of area $A$ is $\Phi_{21} = B_1 A = \mu_0 n_1 I_1 A$. Total linkage with coil 2 ($N_2 = n_2 l$ turns) is $\lambda_2 = N_2 \Phi_{21} = (n_2 l)(\mu_0 n_1 I_1 A) = (\mu_0 n_1 n_2 A l)I_1$. Mutual inductance is $M = \lambda_2 / I_1 = \mu_0 n_1 n_2 A l$. By reciprocity theorem, $M_{12} = M_{21} = M$.
formulas.description: Mutual inductance between two co-axial solenoids and coupling coefficient $k = M/\sqrt{L_1 L_2} \le 1$.
formulas.explanation: For perfectly coupled coils with zero flux leakage, $k = 1$ and $M = \sqrt{L_1 L_2}$.

formulas.latex: i(t) = I_0 (1 - e^{-t / \tau_L}) \quad (\text{Growth}), \quad i(t) = I_0 e^{-t / \tau_L} \quad (\text{Decay}), \quad \tau_L = \frac{L}{R}
formulas.title: Transient LR Circuit Growth and Decay
formulas.derivation: KVL during growth: $\mathcal{E} - L\frac{di}{dt} - iR = 0 \implies L\frac{di}{dt} = \mathcal{E} - iR$. Separating variables: $\frac{di}{\mathcal{E} - iR} = \frac{dt}{L}$. Integrating with $i(0) = 0$: $-\frac{1}{R}\ln\left(1 - \frac{iR}{\mathcal{E}}\right) = \frac{t}{L} \implies i(t) = \frac{\mathcal{E}}{R}\left(1 - e^{-Rt/L}\right)$.
formulas.description: Time-dependent current build-up and decay in inductive RL circuit with inductive time constant $\tau_L = L/R$.
formulas.explanation: At $t = \tau_L = L/R$, current reaches $63.2\%$ of steady value $I_0$; inductor acts as open-circuit at $t=0^+$ and short-circuit as $t \to \infty$.

formulas.title: Root-Mean-Square (RMS) Values of Sinusoidal AC
formulas.derivation: For $i(t) = I_0 \sin(\omega t)$, Joule heat generated in resistor $R$ over one period $T = 2\pi/\omega$ is $H = \int_0^T i^2(t) R dt$. An equivalent DC current $I_{rms}$ dissipates identical heat: $I_{rms}^2 R T = R \int_0^T I_0^2 \sin^2(\omega t) dt$. Since the average of $\sin^2(\omega t)$ over full period is $\frac{1}{2}$: $I_{rms}^2 T = I_0^2 \left(\frac{T}{2}\right) \implies I_{rms} = \frac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}}$.
formulas.description: Effective heating value of alternating sinusoidal current and voltage over full periodic cycle.
formulas.explanation: Standard wall outlet voltages (e.g., $230\text{ V}$ or $120\text{ V}$) always quote RMS values; peak voltage is $V_0 = \sqrt{2}V_{rms}$ ($325\text{ V}$ for $230\text{ V}$).

formulas.latex: Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}, \quad X_L = \omega L, \quad X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C}
formulas.title: Impedance of Series LCR Circuit
formulas.derivation: Phasor analysis: current phasor $\tilde{I}$ is common in series loop. Resistor voltage $\tilde{V}_R = I R$ is in phase with current. Inductor voltage $\tilde{V}_L = I X_L$ leads current by $+90^\circ (+i)$. Capacitor voltage $\tilde{V}_C = I X_C$ lags current by $-90^\circ (-i)$. Total complex voltage is $\tilde{V} = \tilde{V}_R + \tilde{V}_L + \tilde{V}_C = I [R + i(X_L - X_C)]$. Impedance magnitude is $Z = |\tilde{V}|/I = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}$.
formulas.description: Total opposition to sinusoidal alternating current flow combining resistance, inductive reactance, and capacitive reactance.
formulas.explanation: Phase angle between voltage and current is $\tan\phi = \frac{X_L - X_C}{R}$.

formulas.title: Resonant Frequency and Quality Factor (Q) of Series LCR
formulas.derivation: Current amplitude is $I_0 = \frac{V_0}{\sqrt{R^2 + (\omega L - 1/\omega C)^2}}$. Current is maximized when reactive term vanishes: $\omega L - \frac{1}{\omega C} = 0 \implies \omega_0^2 = \frac{1}{LC} \implies \omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$. At resonance, impedance is purely resistive ($Z_{min} = R$) and current is in phase with voltage ($\cos\phi = 1$). Quality factor is $Q = \frac{\omega_0 L}{R} = \frac{1}{R}\sqrt{\frac{L}{C}} = \frac{\omega_0}{\Delta\omega}$ where $\Delta\omega$ is bandwidth at half-power points.
formulas.description: Condition for minimum impedance, maximum current resonance, and sharpness factor of resonance curve.
formulas.explanation: High $Q$ produces extremely sharp tuning selectivity in radio receivers and RF filter circuits.

formulas.title: Average AC Power and Power Factor
formulas.derivation: Instantaneous power is $p(t) = v(t)i(t) = [V_0 \sin(\omega t)][I_0 \sin(\omega t - \phi)] = V_0 I_0 \sin(\omega t)[\sin\omega t\cos\phi - \cos\omega t\sin\phi] = V_0 I_0 [\sin^2\omega t\cos\phi - \sin\omega t\cos\omega t\sin\phi]$. Averaging over a full cycle: $\langle \sin^2\omega t \rangle = 1/2$ and $\langle \sin\omega t\cos\omega t \rangle = 0$. Hence $P_{avg} = \frac{1}{2}V_0 I_0 \cos\phi = \left(\frac{V_0}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\left(\frac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\cos\phi = V_{rms} I_{rms} \cos\phi$. From impedance triangle, $\cos\phi = R/Z$.
formulas.description: Real active power dissipated in AC circuit over complete cycle governed by phase angle $\phi$.
formulas.explanation: For purely reactive circuits (pure $L$ or pure $C$), $\phi = \pm 90^\circ \implies \cos\phi = 0$, giving zero real power dissipation (wattless current).

formulas.title: Ideal Transformer Voltage, Current and Turns Ratio
formulas.derivation: Assuming ideal core with zero flux leakage: common flux $\Phi$ links both windings. Induced EMFs are $V_p = -N_p \frac{d\Phi}{dt}$ and $V_s = -N_s \frac{d\Phi}{dt}$. Dividing gives $\frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p}$. For an ideal lossless transformer (100% efficiency), input power equals output power: $V_p I_p = V_s I_s \implies \frac{I_p}{I_s} = \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p}$.
formulas.description: Transformation of AC voltage and current in magnetically coupled primary and secondary windings.
formulas.explanation: Step-up transformer ($N_s > N_p$): voltage increases and current decreases proportionately, minimizing $I^2 R$ transmission line losses.

formulas.latex: \omega_{LC} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}, \quad q(t) = Q_0 \cos(\omega_{LC} t), \quad i(t) = -\omega_{LC} Q_0 \sin(\omega_{LC} t)
formulas.title: LC Tank Circuit Oscillations
formulas.derivation: Total circuit energy is $E = U_E + U_B = \frac{q^2}{2C} + \frac{1}{2}Li^2$. In lossless circuit, $\frac{dE}{dt} = 0$: $\frac{q}{C}\frac{dq}{dt} + L i \frac{di}{dt} = 0$. Since $i = \frac{dq}{dt}$, dividing by $i$ gives $\frac{q}{C} + L\frac{d^2q}{dt^2} = 0 \implies \frac{d^2q}{dt^2} + \frac{1}{LC}q = 0$. This is standard SHM equation with $\omega_{LC} = 1/\sqrt{LC}$. Solution with initial charge $Q_0$ is $q(t) = Q_0\cos(\omega t)$.
formulas.description: Undamped harmonic exchange of energy between electric field of capacitor and magnetic field of inductor.
formulas.explanation: Energy sloshes sinusoidally between all-electric state ($U_E = Q_0^2/2C$) and all-magnetic state ($U_B = \frac{1}{2}L I_{max}^2$).

formulas.title: Maxwell's Displacement Current
formulas.derivation: Between capacitor plates during charging, no conduction electrons flow, yet magnetic field exists. Electric field is $E = \frac{Q}{\epsilon_0 A} \implies Q = \epsilon_0 E A = \epsilon_0 \Phi_E$. Differentiating charge with respect to time: $I_c = \frac{dQ}{dt} = \epsilon_0 \frac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$. Maxwell recognized this time-varying flux term acts as an effective displacement current $I_d = \epsilon_0 \frac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$, restoring Ampere's law to $\oint \vec{B}\cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0 (I_c + I_d)$.
formulas.description: Equivalent current arising from time-varying electric flux, completing Ampere-Maxwell law.
formulas.explanation: Displacement current between plates exactly equals conduction current in the connecting wires ($I_d = I_c$), ensuring continuity.

formulas.title: Speed of Electromagnetic Waves in Vacuum and Field Ratio
formulas.description: Propagation velocity of light from Maxwell's equations and relation between electric and magnetic field amplitudes.
formulas.explanation: Proved that light is an electromagnetic transverse wave propagating at universal speed $c$.

formulas.derivation:
Albert Einstein postulated light energy arrives in discrete quantized packets (photons) of energy $E = h
u$. An electron absorbs a single photon: portion of energy $\phi$ overcomes surface binding potential barrier (work function); remainder appears as maximum kinetic energy: $h
u = \phi + K_{max} \implies K_{max} = h
